fills.name: Berserker
fills.quote: And we can build berserkers in dark age. 75 40 gold, 22 second production time.
fills.note: Beasty reads the in-game card (YouTube auto-captions). Valdy agrees at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DGW0mPhA4do&t=683s: '75 food and and 40 gold'. RTS_Papercut: 'A Berserker is only 115' resources.
fills.verdictReason: The video's English auto-captions (title 'Everything You Need to Know About Vikings in Age of Empires IV') say at 516.6-521.7s: 'And we can build berserkers in dark age. 75 40 gold, 22 second production time.' The 75 is given as part of the Berserker cost, but the speaker never names its resource. Only the 40 is labelled 'gold'. Reading 75 as food is a likely inference from the usual AoE4 infantry cost pattern, but the page does not say 'food', and the source is ASR captions. Refuted because the field is inferred. No correctedValue: the page gives no other food value.

fills.name: Berserker
fills.quote: Veteran berserkers right here. 15 damage. So 16 when you complete the plus two attack
fills.verdictReason: I pulled the video's English auto-captions with yt-dlp. At 33:12-33:22 the speaker says "Veteran berserkers right here. 15 damage. So 16 when you complete the plus two attack", reading Castle Age unit stats. So the quote is real, but 15 is not the base Veteran Berserker damage. At 29:23-29:34 the speaker says the auto-researched upgrade already gave all units "plus one ... cavalry, infantry, archer attack", and "16 when you complete the plus two attack" (one more point per tier) confirms that the 15 shown includes the +1 attack tier. Recording 15 as the unit's damage mixes the on-screen value after an upgrade with the base stat. The video never states the base Veteran damage outright. It is implied to be 14, so no correctedValue is given. Also, earlier at 17:55 Hardened berserkers are said to "do 12 damage" in Feudal, before any attack upgrade.

fills.name: Bondi
fills.quote: What the what? 159 move speed. Holy. These are the spears. 144 move speed.
fills.note: Valdy also says 'They move at 144'. No base speed was stated specifically for the Bondi; Valdy's '125' refers to 'a spear' in general.
fills.verdictReason: I checked the YouTube auto-captions (en-orig, fetched with yt-dlp). At 21:24-21:32 the streamer says: "What the what? 159 move speed. Holy. These are the spears. 144 move speed." Earlier lines tie Bondi to the spear unit: "Produces bondi spearman" (5:35) and "Let's upgrade the spearman. Bondi will go to 105 HP" (17:24). So the video does show 144 (read as 1.44) for the Feudal spear/Bondi. The claim's variant "with Turnshoes" is not supported, though. The word "Turnshoes" never appears in the transcript. The only related line is at 20:23, where the streamer reads an unnamed barracks tech: "Increases melee infantry move speed by 15% and charge damage by 30%". It is never said that this tech was researched before the 144 reading; "Let's get that hammer" (20:33) is ambiguous. Linking 1.44 to this tech requires outside math: an assumed 1.25 base speed x 1.15 = 1.44. The video does not state it. The number fits Bondi's displayed Feudal speed, but the upgrade name and the claim that it was applied are guesses, so the claim as labelled is refuted. It could be relabelled as "Feudal Bondi speed shown in stream, after the +15% melee infantry speed barracks tech was viewed (unnamed, research not confirmed)". I could not download frames to check the screen: the video formats were blocked by YouTube's n-challenge.

fills.name: Longship
fills.quote: This is a archer ship aka the snoot ship. Five burst attacks. So this is their archer ship. 300 HP and they cost 80 150.
fills.note: The cost is spoken as '80 150', which cannot be split into resources reliably. Corvinus: 'Each nonvillager loaded increase health by 30' and 'almost 800 HP in feudo' when loaded. A viewer comment on Beasty's video says it holds up to 16 units, each giving +30 HP and +1 arrow.
fills.verdictReason: I pulled the video's English auto-captions with yt-dlp. The video is 'Everything You Need to Know About Vikings in Age of Empires IV' (nd74LibluQ0). The quoted line is real: at 44:38-44:50 the speaker says 'This is a archer ship aka the snoot ship. Five burst attacks. So this is their archer ship. 300 HP and they cost 80 150.' So 300 HP belongs to the Vikings archer ship, which he calls the 'snoot ship'. He never names that ship 'Longship'. 'Long ships' comes up only later, at 46:16-46:24, when he reads an upgrade: 'Increases the whole size of long ships by six... Wait, so long ships are also transport ships.' Nothing links that name to the 300 HP archer ship. 'Snoot ship' may be a mis-captioned unit name, such as Snekkja, which would make the Longship a different ship. The axe-throwing ship at 44:55-45:17 is another candidate. Calling the 300 HP ship 'Longship' is a guess, so I marked the claim refuted. The video gives no HP for an object it names 'Longship'.

fills.name: Hamrammr
fills.quote: Berserker gang triggers at 50% health and heals for 50% more
fills.note: Read from the Barracks tech list in Feudal, right after Beasty says 'what else do we have in barracks?'. GiveUAnxiety: 'This is an age two upgrade'.
fills.verdictReason: The page loaded: Beastyqt, 'Everything You Need to Know About Vikings in Age of Empires IV'. Its title, description and chapter list never mention Hamrammr, Barracks or Berserker (0 occurrences in the full page HTML). The caption and transcript endpoints returned empty or 400, so the spoken audio at 20:39 could not be checked. The claimed quote only describes a Berserker ability (triggers at 50% health, heals 50% more) and says nothing about which building the Hamrammr comes from. So 'building = Barracks' is not stated by the source and looks inferred or guessed.

fills.name: Hagl Brodda
fills.quote: Um, and we got a new archer upgrade. Haggle Balda. The archer unleashes a hail of arrows when attacking, firing two additional arrows at random nearby locations. They do three less damage.
fills.note: Beasty finds it at the Archery Range in Castle Age, next to the Skâne Crossbowman.
fills.verdictReason: I fetched the transcript for nd74LibluQ0 myself (1,170 caption lines). At 32:30-32:43 it says only: "we got a new archer upgrade. Haggle Balda. The archer unleashes a hail of arrows when attacking, firing two additional arrows at random nearby locations. They do three less damage." Nothing in that passage names the building where it is researched. The line before it is "Archers." (32:17), and before that the speakers are at the "barracks" (31:53) buying the Bondi/Berserker/men-at-arms upgrades. The words "archery range" never appear in the transcript; the only near match is "archer range" at 18:41, which has nothing to do with this upgrade. "Archery Range" therefore looks like a guess, and the transcript gives no other building to correct it to.

fills.name: Farmathr
fills.quote: Traders will make a couple, but I assume uh Oh, there is an upgrade. Pharmathur increases trader and trade ships health by 25% and move speed by 10%.
fills.note: Beasty had just aged to Feudal. GiveUAnxiety also sees it in Age II.
fills.verdictReason: I fetched the transcript (1170 segments). At 1148-1156s the quoted line appears: "Oh, there is an upgrade. Pharmathur increases trader and trade ships health by 25% and move speed by 10%." It gives only the effect. Nowhere in the video is Farmathr tied to an age. The speaker had reached Feudal Age shortly before (1054s, "upgraded to feudal age now"), so 'Feudal' is an inference from when he happened to notice the tech. The video never states it as the tech's required age. That makes the claimed value a guess, not a stated number.

fills.name: Farmstead (Longhouse attachment)
fills.quote: Ah, these take 20 seconds and these take two seconds.
fills.note: Bee Skeps take 20 s and Farmstead 2 s. Drongo: 'if you're interested in going into a farmstead, that only takes 2 seconds'.
fills.verdictReason: The video's English auto-captions do contain the quote at 815.0s: "Ah, these take 20 seconds and these take two seconds." But nothing in it ties either figure to the Farmstead. Just before it, at 809s, the speaker says "let's upgrade these B skips" (Beekeep), and right after he says the attachment gives 50 gold per minute and costs 200 wood, which is the Beekeep. He does not say which "these" takes 2 s and which takes 20 s. They could be Beekeep vs Farmstead, or two other things on screen, since towers and arrowslits were shown just before. The only remark about Farmstead upgrade speed is at 400s, "Oh, it upgrades fast", with no number. So the 2 s research time for the Farmstead is a guess from an ambiguous quote, and the transcript gives no clear Farmstead research time to offer as a correction.

fills.name: Lion's Duty
fills.quote: lowland technology cost are reduced by 50%. So you can see this is 250 gold and this is 600 food. Infantry gain one armor when near landmark keeps tower houses and stone wall towers
fills.note: GiveUAnxiety (after Stone of Destiny) and Swaggy both say 250. Beasty: Lowland techs cost gold, Highland techs cost food.
fills.verdictReason: I fetched the video's English auto-generated captions (439 lines) and the words 'Lion's Duty' / 'Lion' / 'Duty' never appear. At about 290-310s the speaker says: 'lowland technology cost are reduced by 50%. So you can see this is 250 gold and this is 600 food. Infantry gain one armor when near landmark keeps tower houses and stone wall towers.' The '250 gold' refers to something shown on screen that is never named. The same passage mentions '600 food', which was also the price given at 262s for the Master Pikeman ability. So the captions don't say which object costs 250 gold. Linking 250 gold to Lion's Duty, or to the infantry-armor tech, is a guess. The video gives no value for a tech named Lion's Duty, so there is no corrected value.

fills.name: Stew Ponds
fills.quote: Instantly spawns a free curdle then. It's very 750 gold really expensive upgrade
fills.note: GiveUAnxiety had built Stone of Destiny (Lowland). Effect: +1 fishpond capacity, nearby gather bonus goes from 10% to 20%, and a free Kirkman spawns.
fills.verdictReason: I pulled the video's auto-generated English captions with youtube-transcript-api. At 1493-1510s the speaker does say the 'supon' (Stew Ponds) upgrade 'instantly spawns a free [curdle]. It's very 750 gold really expensive upgrade', so the 750 gold figure is in the video. The claimed variant is not. The video never says this price includes a Lowland landmark discount or any -50% reduction. The only discount mention (1140s) is a general line that powerful technologies get cheaper each time a landmark from a region is chosen, with no percentage. The speaker's Age II landmark was the Stone of Destiny, and the video never says whether that is a Highland or Lowland landmark. Linking the 750 to 'one Lowland landmark (-50%)' is therefore a guess. The video gives no other value for this field, so there is no correction.

fills.name: Feuds Aside
fills.quote: And then the final one is feuds aside. 1,200 food.
fills.note: Beasty gives the undiscounted price: 'So, it cost 2,400 if you didn't go for the highland landmarks'. That matches the checklist's 2400.
fills.verdictReason: The English auto-transcript of the video (youtube-transcript-api, around 940s) does say "And then the final one is feuds aside. 1,200 food.", so the number 1,200 food for Feuds Aside is stated. It is not stated for the claimed variant. The speaker never says the 1,200 figure applies 'with one Highland landmark' and never mentions a -50% discount. He only says the discount depends on your landmark choices. Earlier in the same segment he restarted and went Trilock Lookout, so which landmark state the 1,200 reflects is not identified in the speech. The variant and discount percentage are inferences the video does not state, so the claim as written is not supported. No different value is stated for that variant.

fills.verdictReason: I fetched the English auto-generated transcript with youtube_transcript_api (619 lines). At 1438.2-1447.2 s it says: "In the university, we have everything the same, except for the hand cannon upgrade, which is basically the same thing, but it just says that it affects border rivers as well." The words "Snaphance" and "lock" (as a tech name) appear nowhere in the transcript. The video places an unnamed "hand cannon upgrade" in the University. fills.name: Highland Ambush
fills.quote: Now in addition to that, you're also going to pick up an extra 10% movement speed, 1.38 compared to being outside of it.
fills.note: +10% infantry move speed in stealth forests, with no vision penalty there. Clan Traditions adds 10 s to the bonus duration ('Highland ambush bonus duration is increased by 10 seconds').
fills.verdictReason: The quote is real: at 1:57 the transcript says "you're also going to pick up an extra 10% movement speed, 1.38 compared to being outside of it". But the speaker is describing the civ bonus "infantry have vision and movement speed bonuses while in stealth forests", and he never calls it Highland Ambush there. His own baseline is hedged ("I think it's 1.25 outside of that"). The only place the video uses the name is at 15:17, in the Clan Traditions upgrade: "Highland ambush bonus duration is increased by 10 seconds". That describes a timed bonus. Linking the in-forest 10% speed to the Highland Ambush effectValue is therefore the claimant's inference, not something the video states. The video gives no other effect value for Highland Ambush. The 10 seconds is a duration increase from an upgrade, a different field, so there is no correctedValue.

fills.name: Lowland Defensive Network
fills.newItem: Scots civ bonus: dock and naval arrow slits are 50% cheaper
fills.note: Corvinus and Drongo also mention it.
fills.verdictReason: The page loaded. The video description has no game stats. In the auto-transcript, at 1:08 the narrator reads the general Scots civ bonuses aloud: 'Destroyed keeps create a scorched earth effect... Naval arrows slits are 50% cheaper.' The quote matches word for word, but it is part of an unnamed list of civ bonuses. The phrase 'Lowland Defensive Network' never appears in the transcript: there are no hits for 'defens' or 'network'. The page therefore does not tie the 50% to an object with that name, so the attribution to that name and the effectValue field is unsupported. The ASR text is also garbled ('Naval arrows slits'), and at 4:41 a separate line says 'arrow slit emplacement cost reduced by 50%'. The 50% figure is stated, so I give no correctedValue; the problem is which object it belongs to.
